scope: Actual finite-cutoff independent-link Wilson integration, source transport, and weak-coupling obstructions. Mathematical derivations below are not included in the Lean-certified count unless explicitly linked to a declaration.

conventions.lattice: Periodic n^4 lattice; SU(2) derivations assume n>=3, checkerboard n even >=4.
conventions.action: S_beta(U)=beta*S0(U), S0=sum_p (2-ReTr U_p), with normalized product Haar and beta>=0.
conventions.counts: L=4*n^4 positive links and P=6*n^4 unoriented plaquettes.
conventions.quaternion: For an oriented selected link, define a_e in R^4 by ReTr(g A_e)=2*q(g) dot a_e. This uses the conjugate quaternion coordinates of the raw staple matrix sum A_e. r_e=|a_e|<=6.
conventions.one_link: Conditionally on all exterior links, the action is C-2*beta*q dot a_e. E=S-min S=kappa*(1-q0), kappa=2*beta*r_e after Haar rotation.
conventions.not_a_continuum_identification: No coupling trajectory, observable mixing, infinite-volume continuum field, or physical mass scale is supplied by these finite formulas.

content: Independent means disjoint actual affected-plaquette sets.
A full parallel coordinate line has exactly n independent selected links.
Transverse nearest-neighbor separation gives an independence criterion.
Actual Wilson action and arbitrarily weighted real plaquette observables decompose into singleton changes.
WilsonIndependentBlocks.restriction: An independent block is conditional on the exterior. No independence of retained links after integration is asserted.

content: Product Haar integration of the actual sourced block action factors exactly into single-link partitions and the reference-configuration prefactor.
The first logarithmic source derivative is the actual reference source plus the sum of conditional source increments.
The second logarithmic derivative and actual sourced fixed-exterior Gibbs variance equal the sum of single-link variances. Compactness supplies differentiation bounds.
WilsonBlockIntegration.domain: Any compact second-countable topological group with Borel Haar measure and a continuous character function; no SU(2) quaternion formula is built into these formal theorems.
WilsonBlockIntegration.auxiliary_coordinates: The integral is indexed by all positive link coordinates, while the block update ignores unselected auxiliary coordinates. Their Haar integrals equal one.

exact_su2_step.independent_checkerboard: Fix direction mu and select bases whose sum of transverse coordinates is even. On an even torus, transverse stepping flips this parity. A plaquette contains at most one selected mu-link.
exact_su2_step.partition: J(b)=integral_{S3} exp(b dot q) d sigma(q). For real b, J(b)>0; for complex b the entire series is sum_{j>=0}(b dot b/4)^j/[j!*(j+1)!]. In particular J(0)=1 and there is no singularity at a cancelling staple.
exact_su2_step.block_excess: Under fixed exterior, selected-link excess energies are independent. E exp(t*sum_e E_e)<= (1-t)^(-3*|B|/2) for 0<=t<1, using the previously derived one-link Gamma domination.
exact_su2_step.retained_action: S_eff=beta*sum_{p untouched}(2-ReTr U_p)+sum_{e selected}[12*beta-log J(2*beta*a_e)]. Constants follow from six incident plaquettes per selected link.
exact_su2_step.normalized_source: For trace sources J_p, b_e(J)=sum_{p incident e}J_p*a_{e,p}. With the actual unsourced retained marginal nu_eff, Z(J)/Z(0)=E_nu_eff exp[sum_{p untouched}J_p ReTr U_p + sum_e(log J(2*(beta*a_e+b_e(J)))-log J(2*beta*a_e))]. Defect sources add their constants and change the trace-source sign.
exact_su2_step.locality: Each first-step factor depends on at most18 retained exterior links. Its support contains opposite-parity parallel links at x+nu and x-nu; those links are coupled by the generated factor.
exact_su2_step.nonclosure: The resulting action is not assumed to have Wilson plaquette form. Reapplying the original opposite-parity product rule would be invalid.

sharp_one_link_covariance.status: Complete natural-math derivation independently checked by two agents; sphere/Haar and series bridges not yet Lean-certified.
sharp_one_link_covariance.claim: For d sigma_b(q)=exp(b dot q)/J(b) d sigma(q) on S3, 0<=Cov_b(q)<=I/4. If kappa=|b|>0, Cov_b(q)<=I/kappa also.
proof: Normalized Haar on S3 has q0 density (2/pi)*sqrt(1-q0^2) on [-1,1]. Its even moments M_j obey M_0=1 and M_j=(2j-1)/(2j+2)*M_{j-1}, by integration by parts. Thus M_j=(2j)!/[4^j*j!*(j+1)!].
Writing a_j=1/[4^j*j!*(j+1)!], J(kappa)=sum_j a_j*kappa^(2j). Factorial convergence justifies locally uniform differentiation and sums weighted by j.

Let m=J_prime/J and t=m/kappa. The radial and transverse Hessian eigenvalues of log J are v=m_prime=Var(q0)>=0 and t. Differentiating the positive series gives J_prime/kappa=sum_j c_j*a_j*kappa^(2j), c_j=1/[2*(j+2)].

Therefore t is the expectation of the decreasing sequence c_j under probabilities proportional to a_j*kappa^(2j). It is <=1/4 and t_prime=(2/kappa)*Cov(j,c_j)<=0. The covariance sign follows by expanding twice the covariance as the sum of w_i*w_j*(i-j)*(c_i-c_j).
Consequently v=t+kappa*t_prime<=t<=1/4. Since m<=1, t<=1/kappa. At kappa=0, J=1+kappa^2/8+O(kappa^4), so Hessian log J=I/4.
The earlier Gamma excess-energy domination also gives v<=15/(4*kappa^2). This sharper radial estimate is separate from the transverse 1/kappa bound.
sharp_one_link_covariance.weighted_defect_source: For a_p=c*(1-v_p dot q), c=2 for repo trace or1 for normalized trace, action beta*sum a_p, and real weights f_p, sd_cond(sum f_p*a_p)<=sqrt(15)*|f0|/(2*beta)+(c/2)*sum_p|f_p-f0|. Proof: split f0*sum a_p plus the remainder; use Gamma for the first term and Cov(q)<=I/4 for the remainder, then centered L2 triangle.
sharp_one_link_covariance.gradient_scope: If all six coefficients sample the same smooth scalar test nearby, the remainder is O(a*norm(grad f)). A source supported in one plaquette orientation does not automatically have this small remainder.

averaged_bad_staples.status: Complete mathematical derivation, independently checked; not Lean-certified.
averaged_bad_staples.claim: For any link and0<=r0<6, P_Wilson(r_e<=r0)<=min(1,3*A_beta/[(6-r0)*beta]). At r0=3 this is min(1,A_beta/beta), independent of n.
proof: Use SU(2) bi-invariant angular distance theta from identity. Its normalized Haar angle density is (2/pi)*sin(theta)^2. For delta=1/(4*sqrt beta), sin theta>=2*theta/pi on[0,delta], giving cap mass>=8*delta^3/(3*pi^3)=C^(-1)*beta^(-3/2).

When every link lies in the cap, the triangle inequality bounds every plaquette angle by4*delta. Its unnormalized trace defect2*(1-cos theta) is <=theta^2<=1/beta. Therefore Z_beta>=exp(-P)*(C^(-1)*beta^(-3/2))^L.
Relative entropy of exp(-beta*S0)/Z_beta against probability Haar is -beta*E_Wilson S0-log Z_beta>=0. Hence beta*E S0<=-log Z_beta<=P+L*log C+(3/2)*L*log beta.
Translations, coordinate permutations and orientation invariance of real SU(2) trace give the same mean defect for all plaquettes. Since L/P=2/3, E defect<=A_beta/beta.
The sum of the six incident defects equals12-2*q dot a_e and is at least12-2*r_e. On r_e<=r0 it is at least2*(6-r0). Its expectation is <=6*A_beta/beta; Markov yields the claim.
averaged_bad_staples.probe_bound: For O_b=2*b dot q with exterior-measurable |b|<=B, Var_cond(O_b)<=|b|^2*min(1,2/(beta*r_e)), treating r_e=0 by the first bound. Therefore E_Wilson Var_cond(O_b)<=B^2*min(1,(A_beta+2/3)/beta), using r0=3.
averaged_bad_staples.optimized_threshold: The same split optimized at r0=6/[1+sqrt(3*A_beta/2)] gives B^2*min(1,[sqrt(1/3)+sqrt(A_beta/2)]^2/beta).
averaged_bad_staples.scope: This proves a normalized actual-model averaged local source remainder. It does not bound the covariance of retained conditional means, source-tilted marginals, or repeated RG transformations.

finite_source_remainder.status: Mathematical consequence of the sharp covariance bound; not Lean-certified.
finite_source_remainder.definition: Phi(v)=log J(2*v), v=beta*a. R(v,b)=Phi(v+b)-Phi(v)-gradient Phi(v) dot b.
finite_source_remainder.good_region: If r>=r0>0 and |b|<=beta*r0/2, every segment point has |v+s*b|>=beta*r0/2. Hessian Phi<=4/(beta*r0)*I, so R<=2*|b|^2/(beta*r0).
finite_source_remainder.averaged: For exterior-dependent b bounded by B and B<=beta*r0/2, E_original_retained R<=B^2*(2/(beta*r0)+(1/2)*P(r<r0)).
finite_source_remainder.limitation: An expectation bound for a local remainder cannot be exponentiated into a bound on log E exp(sum R). Source tilting and joint tails still need control.

worst_boundary_obstruction.status: Explicit actual-model construction and derivation; not Lean-certified.
worst_boundary_obstruction.geometry: Set all transverse links to identity. The six opposite parallel links based at x+/-e_nu, nu!=mu, are distinct for n>=3 and independently determine the six selected-link staples (up to inversion).
worst_boundary_obstruction.construction: Set five staples to diag(exp(2*pi*i*k/5),exp(-2*pi*i*k/5)), k=0,...,4. They sum to zero. Vary the sixth opposite parallel exterior link from I to -I, leaving all others unchanged. The staple sum switches between+I and-I.
worst_boundary_obstruction.conditional_laws: The selected link then has density proportional to exp(+/-2*beta*q0). Their TV distance equals1-2*P_plus(q0<0).
worst_boundary_obstruction.bound: Let kappa=2*beta. Gamma(3/2,rate1) domination of E=kappa*(1-q0) gives TV>=1-2*[erfc(sqrt kappa)+(2/sqrt pi)*sqrt kappa*exp(-kappa)], tending to1.
worst_boundary_obstruction.dobrushin: Each of the six exterior-coordinate influence coefficients is at least this TV bound (the maximizing exterior may differ with the coefficient). Thus the supremum Dobrushin row sum exceeds1 for beta>=1. This blocks that particular uniform smallness criterion, not averaged or block methods.
worst_boundary_obstruction.effective_hessian: At a=0, log J(2*beta*a)=beta^2*|a|^2/2-beta^4*|a|^4/24+O(|a|^6), and the Hessian is beta^2*I. Cancelling staples are realized by actual exterior configurations.

remaining_transport_identity.exact: For a source O and retained configuration Y, Var(O)=E Var(O|Y)+Var(E[O|Y]); mixed sources have the corresponding total covariance decomposition.
remaining_transport_identity.controlled: The first-step conditional variance and local finite-source remainder.
remaining_transport_identity.not_controlled: Retained conditional-mean correlations, source-tilted bad-region moments, stability of the generated interaction class and scale-sensitive bounds under repeated integrations. These are required before a nonzero continuum source or physical-energy window can be claimed.

external_statement.summary: Committee reports an OpenAI continuum-existence construction including fermions, based on Wilson/Balaban methods. It leaves confinement and mass gap open and describes validation before release of the Lean proof and1147-page manuscript.
external_statement.effect: No analytic theorem or Lean artifact is supplied in this statement. It changes the external evidence, not this repository certificate.
external_statement.provenance_correction: The previously audited public153-page October6 draft in the Sussman repository is not established to be the committee-held1147-page manuscript. Its identified gaps must not be attributed to the unreleased manuscript.
external_statement.physical_identifications: The announced definition/informal-formal matching review remains essential to importing any eventual theorem; existence alone would not identify this repo's fields, couplings or mass gap.

chessboard_bad_regions.status: Mathematical derivation, independently audited by two agents and checked against the primary chessboard theorem. Not Lean-certified.
chessboard_bad_regions.parameters: Periodic n=4*2^k, k>=1, beta>=1, tile side4; T=(n/4)^4; 0<=r0<6. The case n=4 has a direct one-tile bound, but no chessboard theorem is needed there.

primary_reference.author: Marek Biskup
primary_reference.title: Reflection Positivity and Phase Transitions in Lattice Spin Models
primary_reference.location: Section4.3, Theorem4.8 and event form(4.32), printed pages42-44. All three pages visually inspected.

chessboard_bad_regions.application_is_ours: The reference supplies the general reflection-positive chessboard inequality. Its application to the actual oriented Wilson link measure, star geometry and constants is the derivation below, not a theorem attributed to that reference.
chessboard_bad_regions.claim: For any chosen link e, P_Wilson(r_e<=r0)<=epsilon(beta,r0). For distinct coarse tiles with one specified strictly interior star event each, their joint probability is <=epsilon^m.
proof: Choose direction mu=0 and link(1,2,2,2)->(2,2,2,2) inside closed tile[0,4]^4. All vertices of its six plaquettes lie in{1,2,3}^4, so the star and staple event are strictly interior. Coordinate permutations and a translated tiling cover any selected link.

For each site reflection across coordinate b (a multiple of4), include both fixed planes b and b+n/2. Boundary variables are tangential links lying in those planes. Every remaining link belongs to one of two reflected halves. No unit plaquette has a strict interior vertex on both sides, so S0=S_boundary+S_plus+theta(S_plus). Reflection reversals invert appropriate group variables, preserving Haar and real trace.

Conditional on boundary links, the two half measures are independent and reflection-identical. Hence the reflected quadratic form is the boundary expectation of the squared modulus of a conditional mean, proving reflection positivity for bounded measurable functions in the closed half. No bond-reflection hypothesis is used.

Use reflected copies of the star event in the coarse tiles. They are not silently identified with ordinary translates: normal reflection can reverse a link and change its offset. The quantity2*(6-r_e) is the minimum over U_e of the six-plaquette defect sum, hence is invariant under those reflection/orientation changes.
The disseminated star plaquette sets are disjoint. All T events therefore force S0>=2*(6-r0)*T. Their joint probability is at most exp[-2*(6-r0)*beta*T]/Z_beta.

The previously proved cap lower partition gives -log Z_beta<=6*n^4+4*n^4*log(24*pi^3)+6*n^4*log beta. Divide byT=n^4/256 and apply the chessboard inequality. This gives exactly the stated C_beta and no volume dependence.

The multi-event version applies a separate disseminated bound to each chosen block function. It gives the joint epsilon^m estimate even for different specified interior stars in distinct tiles, since each full dissemination has the same energy cost.
chessboard_bad_regions.exponential_moment: For the chosen tile events A_t and s_t>=0, E exp(sum_t s_t*1_A_t)<=prod_t[1+epsilon*(exp(s_t)-1)]. Expand the product into subsets and apply the joint probability bound. In particular E exp(s*N_bad)<=[1+epsilon*(exp(s)-1)]^T.
chessboard_bad_regions.probe_improvement: At r0=3, the averaged trace-probe variance is <=B^2*min(1,2/(3*beta)+epsilon(beta,3)); thus it is O(1/beta) on this lattice family. Constants are deliberately crude, so the exponential bound becomes useful only at sufficiently large beta.
chessboard_bad_regions.actual_insertion_mean: Put delta=6-r. The same result for every threshold gives P(delta>=t)<=min(1,exp[C_beta-2*beta*t]). With u=C_beta/(2*beta), delta is dominated by u+Exp(rate2*beta), so E delta^2<=u^2+u/beta+1/(2*beta^2). For fixed real six-plaquette weights f, Y_f=E[sum f_p*a_p|exterior] satisfies |Y_f|<=norm(f)_infty*(2*delta+3/(2*beta)). Consequently norm(Y_f)_L2<=norm(f)_infty*(C_beta+sqrt(2)+3/2)/beta. This is an actual one-step effective-source mean bound.
limits: The even dyadic family is not automatically the odd lattice/blocking family used in a given Balaban construction. A regulator comparison is needed before such an import.
These are microscopic Wilson star events and the original Wilson probability measure. They have not been identified with all bad multiscale histories or proved stable under arbitrary source tilts.
The exponential moment controls these bad-event counts; it does not by itself bound arbitrary source remainders or retained source correlations.

common_vacuum_subtraction.status: New natural-math derivation independently checked; not Lean-certified. This is one exact conditional-integration step, not a multiscale history theorem.
common_vacuum_subtraction.setting: A_e(U)=sum of the six incident unnormalized plaquette defects. beta>0, r=|a_e|, kappa=2*beta*r, h(kappa)=E_kappa[kappa*(1-q0)]. Set h(0)=0.
common_vacuum_subtraction.identity: E[A_e|exterior]=12-2*r+h(kappa)/beta. The retained nonlinear insertion is A_min=12-2*r.
common_vacuum_subtraction.sphere_ibp: Integrating the derivative of exp(kappa*x)*(1-x^2)^(3/2) over[-1,1] gives kappa*E(1-q0^2)=3*E q0. Substitute q0=1-E/kappa to get2*kappa*(h-3/2)=E[E^2]-3*h.
common_vacuum_subtraction.bound: Gamma domination gives0<=h<=3/2. Since E[E^2]>=0,0<=3/2-h<=(3*h)/(2*kappa)<=9/(4*kappa) for kappa>0.
common_vacuum_subtraction.subtraction: Subtract the SAME vacuum constant3/(2*beta) for every exterior. Then E[A_e|exterior]-3/(2*beta)=A_min+R, R=(h-3/2)/beta.
common_vacuum_subtraction.good_bad_bounds: For r>=3, |R|<=3/(8*beta^2). For r<3, including r=0, |R|<=3/(2*beta).
common_vacuum_subtraction.actual_L2_bound: On the chessboard lattice family, E_Wilson R^2<=9/(64*beta^4)+9*epsilon(beta,3)/(4*beta^2). Thus the source remainder after a common first-step vacuum subtraction is O(beta^(-2)) in L2, while retaining the explicit nonlinear coarse insertion.
common_vacuum_subtraction.unclosed_step: The coarse insertion12-2*r is a nonlinear function of retained links. Its correlations, normalization/mixing across scales and evolution under the generated log J interactions are not yet controlled. A first-step vacuum subtraction is not a proof of a common subtraction across every RG history.

aligned_weighted_fluctuations.parameters: Fixed real six-plaquette weights; fbar=(sum f_p)/6, d_p=f_p-fbar, sum d_p=0. Unit staple coefficient vectors v_p have sum a, r=|a|, delta=6-r.
aligned_weighted_fluctuations.alignment: For r>0 let vhat=a/r. Since sum|v_p-vhat|^2=2*delta, Cauchy-Schwarz gives |sum d_p*v_p|^2<=2*delta*sum d_p^2.
aligned_weighted_fluctuations.good_region: On r>=3 the remainder R_grad=-2*q dot sum d_p*v_p has conditional variance<=4*delta*sum d_p^2/(3*beta). The entropy estimate E delta<=3*A_beta/beta gives its good-region mean<=4*A_beta*sum d_p^2/beta^2.
aligned_weighted_fluctuations.bad_region: The global covariance bound gives Var_cond R_grad<=6*sum d_p^2. On r<3 its mean contribution is <=6*epsilon(beta,3)*sum d_p^2.
aligned_weighted_fluctuations.conclusion: sqrt(E Var_cond(sum f_p*a_p))<=sqrt(15)*|fbar|/(2*beta)+sqrt(4*A_beta/beta^2+6*epsilon(beta,3))*sqrt(sum d_p^2). A source-gradient remainder is now O(beta^(-1)*sqrt(log beta)) in the averaged conditional standard deviation.
aligned_weighted_fluctuations.limits: These weighted fluctuation and common vacuum results concern local incident-plaquette sources. Summation over a growing continuum lattice, contact renormalization and retained conditional-mean correlations remain separate tasks.

weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.status: Complete natural-math first-step derivation, independently reviewed; not Lean-certified.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.definitions: Prescribed real weights f_p; fbar=(sum f_p)/6; d_p=f_p-fbar; d=sum d_p*v_p; D_infty=max|d_p|; D1=sum|d_p|. For r>0 set q_star=a/r; for r=0 set q_star=0. This last convention is a vector convention, not an SU(2) group element.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.coarse_source: G_f=2*sum_p f_p*(1-q_star dot v_p). For r>0 this evaluates the source at the conditional action minimizer. At r=0 it is the Haar average over the degenerate minimizers. G_f is measurable and gauge invariant but is not claimed continuous at r=0.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.identity: Y_f=E[sum f_p*a_p|exterior]=G_f+3*fbar/(2*beta)+R_f, where R_f=fbar*R0+2*(1-m(kappa))*q_star dot d and R0=(h(kappa)-3/2)/beta. The vacuum term depends only on the prescribed weights and coupling, not exterior links.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.good_region: Since sum d_p=0, |q_star dot d|<=D_infty*(6-r). On r>=3, |R_f|<=3*|fbar|/(8*beta^2)+D_infty*(6-r)/(2*beta).
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.bad_region: For r<3, |R_f|<=3*|fbar|/(2*beta)+2*D1. At r=0 the exact gradient contribution is zero under the q_star=0 convention, so no division by r is used.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.L2_bound: With delta=6-r and epsilon>=P(r<3), norm(R_f)_L2<=|fbar|*sqrt(9/(64*beta^4)+9*epsilon/(4*beta^2))+sqrt(D_infty^2*E delta^2/(4*beta^2)+4*D1^2*epsilon). This follows by the L2 triangle inequality and separate good/bad bounds on the gradient contribution.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.chessboard_consequence: For the audited dyadic even lattice family, epsilon<=min(1,exp(C_beta-6*beta)) and E delta^2<=u^2+u/beta+1/(2*beta^2), u=C_beta/(2*beta). Hence the residual is O((|fbar|+D_infty*log beta)/beta^2), plus the displayed exponentially small contribution.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.smooth_source_scope: D_infty and D1 are O(a*norm(grad f)) when the six coefficients sample one isotropic smooth scalar source at nearby plaquettes. No such assertion is made for arbitrary orientation-dependent sources.
weighted_common_vacuum_subtraction.remaining_gap: G_f is a nonlinear retained-link observable; neither a scale-invariant field identification nor stability of its transport under the generated interactions has been proved. Control at every history/scale cannot be inferred from this one-step construction.
